The diffusion process generates synthetic data conditioned on statistical features, mitigating label scarcity. The adaptive loss dynamically adjusts weights based on model performance, improving robustness against class imbalance. These primitives form a dual framework: one for data synthesis and another for dynamic optimization. Failure modes include overfitting to synthetic data or loss weight instability. The spatiotemporal network provides structure for high-dimensional sensor data, but its complexity may hinder deployment. The key insight is that rare events are not just rare in frequency but also in representation; thus, both augmentation and loss design must be tailored to this dual challenge.
